result:
If I'm picking just one thing, I keep landing on something like: making it easier for people to actually understand each other across different experiences and beliefs.

Not in a saccharine "everyone just needs to get along" way, but something more structural—better tools and habits for actually grappling with why someone sees the world differently than you do, without immediately sorting them into "right" or "wrong," "us" or "them." So much harm seems to come from people talking past each other, from contempt substituting for curiosity, from disagreements escalating because nobody feels heard.

I don't think this would eliminate conflict—people have genuinely incompatible interests and values sometimes, and that's real. But I suspect a lot of cruelty and stupidity in the world comes less from people being evil and more from failures of imagination about other people's inner lives. If that gap closed even a little, I think a lot of downstream problems—political dysfunction, prejudice, even some violence—might loosen up too.

That said, I notice this is a very "communication-shaped" answer, maybe because that's the texture of what I actually do. Someone else might reasonably say the one-thing should be more material: ending poverty, curing disease, fixing the climate. I don't think my answer is obviously more important than those—just the one that feels most upstream to me when I try to trace causes back.

What's pulling at you when you think about this question? Curious whether you're drawn toward something structural like this or something more concrete.
